title: How many times taller than a building do eagles and aeroplanes fly?
description: The heights reached by bald eagles, Mount Everest and aeroplanes are each divided by the height of Ziva's forty metre building. A zero is crossed out from both numbers to keep each division short, and the answers are checked by multiplying back.
teaching_notes: One idea: how many times bigger means a height divided by the height of the building, and crossing out a zero from both numbers keeps the answer the same. Watch for students who subtract the heights instead of dividing them.

source: Bald eagles are known to fly as high as 4500 to 6000 m above the ground level. Mount Everest is about 8850 m high. Aeroplanes can fly as high as 10,000 to 12,800 m. How many times bigger are these heights compared to Somu's building?
video_script.why: The child divides a large number by a small one, and now compares several large heights with the height of a building.
video_script.substitution: Divide each height by the height of the building; cross out a zero from both numbers to keep the division short.
video_script.anchor: Ziva's building, 40 m tall, at the left, with a tall bar for each height beside it
video_script.payoff_line: Divide each height by the height of the building

final_answer.value: Eagles 112.5 to 150 times, Everest about 221 times, aeroplanes 250 to 320 times
final_answer.spoken: eagles reach one hundred twelve and a half to one hundred fifty times the height

names.Ziva: the child whose ten floor building, about 40 m tall, is the measure for the comparison

maths_rules: the building has 10 floors of about 4 m each, so it is 40 m tall
how many times bigger = height / 40; cross out a zero from both numbers: 4500 / 40 = 450 / 4

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Think of Ziva's building, with ten floors of about four metres each.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Bald eagles fly as high as four thousand five hundred to six thousand metres.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Mount Everest is about eight thousand eight hundred fifty metres high.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Aeroplanes fly as high as ten thousand to twelve thousand eight hundred metres.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>How many times bigger are these heights than the building?

marks.m1: the heading the bald eagles appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the bald eagles.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four thousand five hundred divided by forty is the same as four hundred fifty divided by four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is one hundred twelve and a half times.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Six thousand divided by forty is six hundred divided by four.
That is one hundred fifty times.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, Mount Everest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Eight thousand eight hundred fifty divided by forty is eight hundred eighty five divided by four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is a little more than two hundred twenty one times.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the aeroplanes.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ten thousand divided by forty is one thousand divided by four, which is two hundred fifty times.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twelve thousand eight hundred divided by forty is one thousand two hundred eighty divided by four.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>That is three hundred twenty times.

marks.m1: the heading check by multiplying back appears
marks.m3: 221 x 40 = 8840 is written, a little under 8850

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check by multiplying back.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred twelve and a half times forty is four thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two hundred twenty one times forty is eight thousand eight hundred forty.
That is a little under the height of Everest.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Three hundred twenty times forty is twelve thousand eight hundred.
